text:
emma_support: :rotating_light: Customer 'MapleAI' just escalated — p95/p99 for /v1/generate jumped from ~220ms/480ms to ~1.8s/3.6s after our maintenance window at 03:50 UTC. They attached traces and request IDs: r-20260317-01, r-20260317-07. Error rate small but latency huge.

alex_oncall: thanks emma. Are these all in eu-west-1? Any host IDs or pod names?

emma_support: yes east-us2/eu-west-1 both seeing it. Sample host from customer trace: host-eu-23, pod gen-5f8a. Logs: "rpc_send: stalled for 1800ms" and some sporadic EIO in dmesg. Link: https://internal/obs/trace/r-20260317-01

jordan_runtime: I saw a similar noise in our canary fleet after the driver/CUDA kernel upgrade last night (cuda 12.1 -> 13.0, driver 545.x). Not sure if kernel or NVMe scheduling is interacting with GPU pagefaults.

maria_infra: getting kernel logs from host-eu-23 now. Preliminary: multiple WARN messages about NVME IO timeout and some soft lockup stacks around hostfs flush. nvme queue depth looks saturated.

srebot: [ALERT] p99 latency anomaly detected on route /v1/generate — 03:52 UTC spike to 3.6s (baseline 480ms) — affected host groups: gen-nodepool-eu, gen-nodepool-us.

alex_oncall: ok next steps — collect: /proc/interrupts, iostat -x 1 5, nvme list && nvme smart-log, dmesg -T, and our runtime logs around the KV cache hits. Also get nvidia-smi and driver version. I'll hit the affected node with a low-impact repro to reproduce tail latency.

emma_support: pasted request IDs and trace links in the ticket. Customer asked for ETA. I'll tell them we're investigating and may move them to dedicated hosts if needed.

jordan_runtime: repro plan (quick): run a short burst of 64 concurrent requests with seq_len 1024 to the same model shard on host-eu-23 while collecting tcpdump and /proc/interrupts. Command:
```
heybench --concurrency 64 --duration 30s --endpoint https://eu.gen.internal/v1/generate -H "x-req-id: repro-20260317"
sudo iostat -x 1 30 > /tmp/iostat.txt &
sudo cat /proc/interrupts > /tmp/interrupts.before
# run repro
sudo cat /proc/interrupts > /tmp/interrupts.after
```

maria_infra: ran iostat and nvme smart-log on host-eu-23: avg await shot up to 12ms from 0.8ms, util 98-100%, Qdepth 64/64. dmesg shows repeated "nvme0: I/O 0x... timed out" then firmware reset. Looks like NVMe throughput saturated under heavy hostfs flushes (KV cache writes).

alex_oncall: that points toward storage contention interacting with the new driver/firmware scheduling. Immediate mitigations: 1) add host-level cgroup to throttle background writes for gen pods 2) move affected customer pods to nodes with older kernel/driver (rollback nodeset) 3) enable KV cache read-only mode to reduce hostfs writes. Which can we do fastest?

maria_infra: we can enable cache read-only mode via config flag on the runtime: 
```
REDWOOD_KV_CACHE_MODE=readonly
systemctl restart redwood-runtime
```
That flips off background spill-to-disk for ~2min change window. I'll push to canary nodes first.

jordan_runtime: also can change async writeback params: `echo 1000 > /proc/sys/vm/dirty_bytes` and lower `vm.dirty_ratio` to reduce write bursts. But that's risky system-wide. Prefer per-pod cgroup blkio throttle:
```
# throttle to 200MB/s for background write cgroup
cgcreate -g blkio:/kvcache_bg
echo "8:0 209715200" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/kvcache_bg/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device
```

ops_lead: approve quick mitigation: enable KV cache readonly on canary and schedule rolling for affected nodepool to older driver image for customers with p99 > 1s. Emma please inform MapleAI we'll attempt a node move tonight at 04:30 UTC if mitigations don't stabilize.

emma_support: will notify, they'll try repro on their side too.

alex_oncall: action items:
- maria to flip KV cache to readonly on 5 canary hosts (in progress)
- jordan to prepare blkio cgroup script and test on staging
- infra to identify nodes with previous driver image for targeted rollback (ops_lead)
- support to update customer at 04:00 and 04:30 windows

maria_infra: KV cache readonly rolled to canary (gen-nodepool-eu-canary-1..3). Early telemetry shows p99 dropping from ~3.2s to ~700ms on canary. Moving to larger set now. :thumbsup:

jordan_runtime: tested blkio throttle in staging, reduced nvme await spikes under concurrency. Plan to apply to bg write cgroup on affected pools after rollout to canary verification.

alex_oncall: good. If canary stabilizes, we'll do rolling remediation: migrate affected customers off hot nodes, then repro with driver downgrade on 10% nodes to confirm root cause. We should also open a vendor support ticket with NVMe/GPU driver vendor including dmesg + smart logs.

ops_lead: assigned ticket INF-2026-0453, vendor contact pinged. Keep slack updated.

emma_support: customer updated — they appreciate the quick action and asked for postmortem. I'll log notes in the incident ticket.

srebot: [RESOLVE] Canary metrics for gen-nodepool-eu-canary show p99 back to 550-750ms after KV cache readonly and throttles. Monitoring set to elevated for 6h.

alex_oncall: we'll keep this thread open for postmortem. Thanks team. :coffee:
